body.statement: As the first D0 obligation, determine whether the synchronizer--two-permutation square satisfies \[\sup_{T\ge1}T^{-1/2}\mathbb E\sup_{(\lambda,\vartheta)\in[0,1]^2}\left|\sum_{t=1}^T m_t(\lambda,\vartheta)\right|<\infty.\] An affirmative answer must give a bound uniform on the entire two-parameter square and then determine whether its predictable-scale argument localizes over every face of \(\Theta(P)\) to prove \[\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|\le \frac{511B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}\sqrt T\quad\text{for every }T\ge1.\] A negative answer must give an explicit horizon-dependent \(\lambda_T,\vartheta_T\) counterselection and derive the sharp replacement rate for \(\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)\) on the unchanged model class.
body.justification: The two-parameter square is the smallest unsolved interior face and the mandatory falsification test for the whole-polytope parametric rate.
body.gap: HaughSingal2026Casino, arXiv version 3, pages 9--11, Sections 4.2--4.3, shows only that in its special casino model the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\); it gives neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber. deLaPenaLaiShao2009 and RakhlinSridharanTewari2015 provide general maximal-inequality tools but do not evaluate this posterior-normalized response-polytope family at vanishing response masses.
body.consumer: The result either supplies the first uniform ingredient for the conditional root-rate theorem or identifies the sharp slower headline rate through a legal face of the same causal model.

obligation.what_is_open: A horizon-uniform two-parameter maximal inequality on the full synchronizer--two-permutation square, followed by a face-localization argument proving the stated \(511B d^{dk}\sqrt{T}/\epsilon\) maximal bound on all of \(\Theta(P)\), remains unproved.
obligation.obstruction: Fixed-parameter martingale concentration and all one-dimensional boundary estimates do not control a parameter chosen from the square after seeing the record. Near the noncontracting corner, transverse derivatives accumulate for order \(T\) steps before damping, so a Euclidean net or an unweighted derivative integral introduces a \(\sqrt{\log T}\) loss. In the full polytope, recursive filtering is polynomial rather than affine in \(q\), so vertex or edge control does not imply control of interior extrema.
obligation.attempted: The exact reparameterization to the triangle \(0\le u\le1\), \(-u\le v\le u\) isolates the two random affine updates and verifies fixed-parameter root-\(T\) control. Abel summation handles the boundary, while direct \(\ell_1\) covering of \(\Theta(P)\) gives only the displayed \(\sqrt{T\log T}\) maximal scale. The direct absolute-value estimate obtained from a two-dimensional fundamental-theorem-of-calculus expansion has a mixed-derivative bound that is not integrable with a horizon-independent constant at the noncontracting corners; this does not rule out a sharper cancellation argument. No legal horizon-dependent counterselection with divergent normalized width has been derived.
obligation.partial_result:
There is a complete reduction, but not a proof of the requested root-\(T\) supremum.  On the synchronizer--two-permutation square set \(Y_t=R_tm_t\), \(u=\lambda\), and \(v=\lambda(2\vartheta-1)\).  Then \(Y_0=1\), the parameter set is the compact triangle
\[
 0\le u\le1,\qquad -u\le v\le u,
\]
and the recursion is exactly
\[
 Y_t=
 \begin{cases}
 1-u+uY_{t-1},&R_{t-1}=1,\\
 1-u+vY_{t-1},&R_{t-1}=-1,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad m_t=R_tY_t.
\]
Thus, for each fixed \((u,v)\), \(m_t\) is a martingale difference and \(|m_t|\le1\).  This proves the fixed-parameter bound
\[
 \mathbb E\left|\sum_{t=1}^T m_t(u,v)\right|\le\sqrt T.
\]
It also identifies the singular geometry that a uniform argument must control: at \((u,v)=(1,1)\), \(Y_t=1\), whereas derivatives transverse to the edge \(v=u\) accumulate the number of negative factual signs before contraction begins.  Boundary Abel summation controls each of the three edges, but it does not control a record-dependent optimizer in the two-dimensional interior.

For the complete polytope, the proved Poisson identity and an \(\ell_1\)-net give the valid fallback
\[
 \mathbb E D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)
 \le \min\left\{1,\frac{2B}{T}
 +B\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2N_T)}{T}}
 +\frac{T+1}{2T^{3/2}}\right\},
 \qquad
 N_T\le\left(1+\frac{4T^{3/2}}{\epsilon}\right)^{d^{dk}}.
\]
Indeed, for \(\delta=\lVert q-q'\rVert_1\), compatibility and the positive-cell condition imply that the total-variation distance between corresponding rows of \(L_q(x,y)\) and \(L_{q'}(x,y)\) is at most \(\delta/(2\epsilon)\).  Telescoping the filtering products gives
\[
 \lVert\alpha_t(q)-\alpha_t(q')\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \frac{t\delta}{2\epsilon},
 \qquad
 |Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}-Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q',T}|
 \le\frac{(T+1)\delta}{4\epsilon}.
\]
The martingale range bound gives the fixed-net-point exponential inequality; maximizing over both signs and over an internal net of radius \(\epsilon T^{-3/2}\), followed by the last Lipschitz display and coarsening domination, yields the stated formula.  Its order is \(\sqrt{\log T/T}\), so it does not settle the OEQ.
